_about.idea: Research runs on history's clock. Each major power has design teams, one to a branch at the start. A branch with one team gets every new design in the month history got it. A second or third team makes the branch's clock run faster ('speed' is months of progress per month for 0, 1, 2 and 3 teams), so its designs arrive early; a branch with no team stands still and falls behind.
_about.effect: What counts in battle is how far a branch is ahead of or behind its own history, in designs: each design in service that history did not yet have is worth 'per' of strength for that branch, each design history had and the nation lacks costs the same, up to 'maxLead' designs either way. A nation that keeps one team on every branch fights exactly as it did, which is how the computer runs every nation.
_about.bureau: A nation can found extra design teams with production points. 'cost' is the price of the first, second and third.
_about.nations: For each major power: 'tree' is the name of its army doctrine; then for every branch its designs in order, each with the month history brought it into service (year-month; anything before September 1939 is in service when the war begins). French entries after June 1940 are the designs France had on the drawing board when it fell.
